entries.title: wrap-up verify: acceptance-labeling check fails on every record-mode run — `gh issue view --json parent` is not a valid field in gh 2.92.0
entries.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js`'s `resolveParent()` (line 392) resolves a record's decomposition parent with `gh issue view {n} --json parent`. On `gh` 2.92.0 (2026-04-28) that field is not in the command's JSON field list, the call throws `Unknown JSON field: "parent"`, and `resolveParent` returns `{ok: false}` — which the `acceptance-labeling` check folds into a `fail` row, so `wrap-up-engine.js verify` exits 3 and `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up`'s Verify step withholds the closure line (`execution-and-verification.md`'s exit-3 rule) on every record-mode run, even when the record's `demo:*` labeling is correct. On `gh` 2.96.0 (this checkout, 2026-09-09) the same command returns `{"parent": null}`, so the failure is version-dependent: any sandbox or machine still on 2.92.x hits it on every run.

Two things are wrong at once. The field choice is fragile — the plugin's other parent/sub-issue resolution (`bin/lib/issues/native-dependencies.js`, `fetchNativeSubIssues`) goes through GraphQL, which exposes `Issue.parent` on every `gh` version that can run GraphQL at all. And the failure class is misreported — every other gather failure in this file (`git status`, `git worktree list`, `git log`, `gh pr view`, lines 172–326) renders `result: 'unknown'`, which the closure line quotes without blocking, while `resolveParent`'s failure alone is rendered as `fail`, turning a tooling gap into a false labeling verdict.

## Deliverables

- Resolve the parent through GraphQL — `gh api graphql` with `repository(owner,name){ issue(number){ parent { number } } }` — through the same `deps.gh` seam the rest of the file uses, so the test double can drive it; keep the resolution in `resolveParent` (or a sibling in `native-dependencies.js` it delegates to) and drop the `--json parent` call.
- When the parent gather itself fails (GraphQL error, unparseable response), render the `acceptance-labeling` row as `result: 'unknown'` with the gather error in `detail`, matching the file's other could-not-gather rows — never `fail`. A real labeling mismatch on a successfully resolved record stays `fail`.
- Extend `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.test.js`: a record whose `deps.gh` GraphQL call returns a parent redirects the labeling check to the parent; a null parent takes the non-parent path; a throwing gather renders `unknown` and does not set exit 3.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `resolveParent` no longer invokes `gh issue view … --json parent`; `grep -n "'--json', 'parent'" plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` returns nothing.
- With a `deps.gh` double that throws `Unknown JSON field: "parent"` (or any error) on the parent lookup, `verify` renders `| acceptance-labeling | unknown | … |` and exits 0 when every other check passes; the closure line quotes the unknown row per `execution-and-verification.md`.
- With a double that returns a parent number, the check reads labels/comments from the parent record; with `parent: null`, from the record itself — both covered by tests.
- `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Add a `parentOf(n)` GraphQL query beside `fetchNativeSubIssues` in `native-dependencies.js` (same `runner` seam, same `{owner, repo}` resolution) and have `resolveParent` call it via `deps.gh(['api', 'graphql', '-f', query, '-F', …])`. In the `acceptance-labeling` check (line ~463), branch on `resolved.ok`: false → return `{ result: 'unknown', detail: resolved.error }` before any label read. Keep the existing `{ok, error}` return shape so the check's other callers are untouched. Tests use the file's existing `deps` injection; no live `gh`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` — `resolveParent` (GraphQL via `deps.gh`), `acceptance-labeling` check's could-not-gather branch
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/native-dependencies.js` — optional `parentOf` helper sharing the GraphQL runner seam
- `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.test.js` — parent-redirect, null-parent, and gather-failure cases
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/execution-and-verification.md` — only if the `unknown` row's closure-line quoting needs the acceptance-labeling case named explicitly

## Gotchas

- Do not "fix" this by pinning a minimum `gh` version: the field works on 2.96 but the plugin runs in sandboxes that install whatever `gh` the image ships; GraphQL is the version-stable path the plugin already relies on elsewhere.
- `unknown` must stay distinct from `skip` (the file's own comment at line 109); a gather failure is not a deliberately skipped check.
- The `deps.gh` double in `engine-verify.test.js` matches on argv — the GraphQL call's argv shape must be stable enough for the existing matcher style, or add one helper the tests can stub by name.

## Original request

wrap-up verify: acceptance-labeling check fails on every record-mode run — `gh issue view --json parent` is not a valid field in gh 2.92.0

**Summary:** `bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js`'s `resolveParent()` calls `gh issue view {n} --json parent`; `gh` 2.92.0 rejects `parent` as an unknown JSON field, so the `acceptance-labeling` row renders `fail` and `verify` exits 3 for any record-mode run, blocking the closure line even when labeling was correct.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` (`resolveParent`, the `acceptance-labeling` check) — `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up`'s Verify execution step

**Repro steps:**
1. On a machine with `gh version 2.92.0 (2026-04-28)`, complete a record-mode `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up` whose `verify-expectations.json` resolves at least one issue number (materialized header or the `issues` key).
2. Run `node bin/wrap-up-engine.js verify --run-dir <run> --base <base>`.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: the `acceptance-labeling` row evaluates the record's parent linkage (null → non-parent path → checks the record's own `demo:*` state / oversight-floor exemption) and passes or fails on the labeling itself.

**Suggested remedy:** resolve the parent the way the plugin already does elsewhere — `bin/lib/issues/native-dependencies.js` / `bin/resolve-blockers.js` use the GraphQL `issue(number:){ parent { number } }` field, which works on this gh version — instead of the REST-backed `--json parent` field the `gh issue view` command does not expose. Also consider distinguishing could-not-gather from a real labeling failure in the row's Result (e.g. `unknown` rather than `fail`), per the skill's own could-not-gather vocabulary.

entries.title: skills/flow, skills/review: skill guidance doesn't warn dispatched subagents that Monitor/background-task notifications never reach them
entries.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

Pipeline skill guidance that instructs starting a background verification loop or subagent
dispatch and then "waiting for the notification" reads naturally as correct for a top-level
interactive session (where Monitor and background-task completion notifications do arrive) but
does not warn that a dispatched subagent (an `Agent`/`Task`-invoked session) never receives such
notifications the way a top-level session does — waiting there hangs indefinitely with no signal
anything is wrong until an external caller intervenes.

Filed via `/claude-tweaks:feedback` at plugin v6.118.0, citing a harness-level
`contract-violation` event log recording 13+ occurrences of an agent narrating "waiting for the
background task/Monitor notification to arrive" and stopping mid-turn across a single build
phase (main session and multiple dispatched subagents), plus 2 more in a separate review/wrap-up
session for the same unit of work — corrected only when an external coordinator explicitly
stated the limitation. `skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md`'s existing "Hung or non-responsive
single-read agent" section (current build, ~line 50) already covers the adjacent but distinct
case of a *reviewing* agent waiting on a *dispatched* agent that goes silent; it does not cover
this record's scenario — a dispatched subagent itself instructed to background a verification
loop and wait for a notification that will never arrive in its own context.

## Deliverables

- Grep this repo's skill directories fresh at build time for every place a skill instructs
  starting a background verification loop, `Monitor`, or subagent dispatch and then "waiting for
  the notification/completion" — this record's own citations (`skills/flow`, `skills/review`)
  are a starting point, not a guaranteed-current file:line list, since guidance text shifts
  between plugin versions (filed against v6.118.0; current build is newer).
- At each such location, state the limitation once, explicitly, near wherever it first
  introduces Monitor or background-task usage for a verification loop or subagent dispatch: a
  dispatched subagent does not receive Monitor or background-task completion notifications the
  way a top-level session does — run long verification loops in the foreground with a generous
  timeout instead of backgrounding them and waiting for a notification, when running as (or
  dispatching) a subagent.
- Do not duplicate the warning at every call site if a shared `_shared/*.md` fragment already
  covers dispatch mechanics for the affected skills (e.g. `_shared/subagent-dispatch-core.md`) —
  add it there once and cite it, per this codebase's own shared-contract-extraction convention,
  if that fragment is already the canonical home for dispatch-mechanics guidance the affected
  skills already cite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every pipeline skill file that currently instructs backgrounding a verification loop or
  subagent dispatch and waiting for a Monitor/background-task notification carries (directly, or
  via a cited shared fragment) an explicit statement that this pattern does not work inside a
  dispatched subagent's own context.
- The added guidance names the correct alternative for a subagent context: run the verification
  loop in the foreground with a generous timeout, not backgrounded.
- A grep for the current call sites is run and cited in the PR description (or commit message)
  as part of this fix, since this record's own file:line citations may be stale relative to the
  build the fix lands on.

## Technical Approach

1. `grep -rln "Monitor\|background" plugin/skills/flow/ plugin/skills/review/` (and any other
   pipeline skill directory instructing background verification loops or subagent dispatch, per
   the record's "Affected component" note) against the actual build this fix lands on — this
   record's own investigation (at v6.123.0) found no literal "Monitor" or "background" hits in
   `skills/flow/*.md`, and only dispatch-adjacent hits in `skills/review/*.md`
   (`step3-lens-dispatch.md`, `code-mode-steps.md`, `step3-routing.md`,
   `step3-debate-and-refutation.md`) — none of which currently state this specific limitation, so
   the guidance gap this record describes is confirmed still open, just not necessarily at the
   exact file:line the original filing cited.
2. Check whether `_shared/subagent-dispatch-core.md` (the shared dispatch-mechanics fragment
   `step3-lens-dispatch.md`'s own header already cites) is the right single home for this
   warning — every pipeline skill dispatching subagents already reads it, so one addition there
   would reach every call site without per-file duplication.
3. Add the warning once, at that shared home (or, if no single shared fragment covers every
   affected call site, at each site directly) — one short paragraph, not a multi-paragraph
   digression.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-dispatch-core.md` — likely single home for the warning, if it
  covers every affected call site
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md` — cites the shared fragment; verify coverage
- `plugin/skills/flow/*.md` — re-grep at build time per Technical Approach step 1

## Gotchas

- Do not add this warning as a blanket disclaimer at the top of every pipeline skill — it only
  applies where a skill actually instructs starting a background loop/dispatch and waiting for a
  notification; a skill with no such instruction gets no warning.
- The original filing's file:line citations are from plugin v6.118.0 — verify against the actual
  build this fix lands on before assuming any specific location still matches (see Technical
  Approach step 1).

## Original request

**Summary:** Pipeline skill guidance that instructs starting a background verification loop or subagent dispatch and then "waiting for the notification" does not warn that a dispatched subagent never receives such notifications the way a top-level session does.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** skills/flow, skills/review (and any other pipeline skill instructing background verification loops or subagent dispatch)

**Use case:** Pipeline skills (e.g. `/claude-tweaks:flow`'s polish/re-verify guidance, `/claude-tweaks:review`'s Step 3 dispatch notes) instruct starting a long-running background command or subagent and then "waiting for the notification" -- phrasing that reads naturally as correct guidance for a top-level interactive session, where Monitor and background-task completion notifications do arrive. This produced a real, repeated, systemic cost on one run I observed, in a private project: the harness's own contract-violation event log recorded 13+ instances of an agent narrating "waiting for the background task/Monitor notification to arrive" and stopping mid-turn across a single build phase (main session and multiple dispatched subagents, none self-corrected mid-run), plus two more in a separate review/wrap-up session for the same unit of work -- corrected only when an external coordinator explicitly stated the limitation. **Suggested resolution:** State the limitation once, explicitly, near wherever a pipeline skill first introduces Monitor or background-task usage for a verification loop or subagent dispatch: a dispatched subagent does not receive Monitor or background-task completion notifications the way a top-level session does -- run long verification loops in the foreground with a generous timeout instead of backgrounding them and waiting for a notification, when running as (or dispatching) a subagent.

**Evidence:** A harness-level contract-violation event log recorded 13+ occurrences during a single build phase's own event log, plus 2 more in a separately-run review/wrap-up session against the same unit of work, before an external correction stopped the pattern. Cost: at minimum two full agent turns spent narrating an unresolvable wait before correction; the build-phase recurrence count suggests a materially larger cost there, uncorrected for the run's duration.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.118.0

Surface: infra

Origin: by:feedback (self-referential session evaluation, /claude-tweaks:feedback bare invocation)

## Current State

#679 ("no evaluation watermark — a second bare /feedback re-judges the whole transcript") shipped a full watermark mechanism (`bin/lib/transcript-judge/watermark.js`, the offset-clause prompt item, `--full`) for the dispatched-judge path. `_shared/transcript-judge.md`'s Degradation section explicitly states: "The self-assessment path never reads or writes a watermark — there is no resolved transcript path to key one on" — carving the self-assessment path out of #679's fix by design. In a session on 2026-09-20/21, the first /claude-tweaks:backlog + /claude-tweaks:feedback sequence's judge dispatch hard-errored on a Fable usage-limit (429) and degraded to self-assessment, which found and filed real findings but wrote no watermark. A second bare /claude-tweaks:feedback invocation later in the same session therefore had no watermark to read, dispatched a fresh judge (this time succeeding, on a resolver-degraded model) against the entire ~3.1MB transcript from byte zero — re-discovering much of the same ground the self-assessment pass had already covered and filed, relying entirely on Step 4's per-item dedup search to avoid re-filing duplicates.

## Deliverables

- Let the self-assessment path write a watermark too, using the same `bytesAtDispatch`/`evaluatedAt`/`filedRecords`/`issueUrls` shape #679 already defined, plus a `mode: "self-assessment"` field so a later consumer (or a human reading the watermark file) can tell it apart from a dispatched judgment — the stated rationale for the current exclusion ("there is no resolved transcript path to key one on") does not actually hold once a transcript did resolve and only the judge dispatch itself failed; that's exactly the scenario this session hit.
- Update `_shared/transcript-judge.md`'s Degradation section and `session-evaluation.md`'s watermark-payload note to reflect the narrower true carve-out (no watermark only when no transcript path resolves at all) rather than the current blanket "self-assessment never writes one."

## Acceptance Criteria

- A self-assessment run that resolves a real transcript path writes a watermark on completion, keyed the same way a dispatched judge's watermark is.
- A subsequent bare /feedback invocation against the same transcript reads that self-assessment-written watermark and scopes its own dispatch via the offset clause, rather than re-judging from byte zero.
- The one true no-watermark case (no transcript path resolves at all — e.g., a sandbox with no accessible transcript store) is still explicitly documented and exempted.

## Release Note

Stopped a failed judge dispatch from forcing a full transcript re-evaluation on the next feedback run.

## Technical Approach

Both `bin/lib/transcript-judge/watermark.js` (confirmed present) and `_shared/transcript-judge.md`'s Degradation section (confirmed carrying the current blanket exclusion at line ~170) already exist and are the two things this record edits — no new mechanism needed. - `plugin/bin/lib/transcript-judge/watermark.js` — the existing watermark read/write shape this record extends to a second caller, not replaces
- `plugin/skills/_shared/transcript-judge.md` — Degradation section (line ~170) carrying the blanket exclusion to narrow
- `plugin/skills/_shared/session-evaluation.md` — the self-assessment degradation flow that needs the new watermark-write call, and the watermark-payload note describing the new `mode` field

- The `mode: "self-assessment"` field is additive to an existing, already-consumed watermark shape — a later reader (the offset-clause logic) must treat an absent `mode` field as the pre-existing dispatched-judge case, not as a new failure mode, so existing watermark files written before this change keep working unread-modified.

entries.title: dispatch: queue-pull-script.md redirects to undeclared $DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED (": No such file or directory" on every pull)
entries.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md:294` runs `echo '[]' > "$DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED"` in the open-linked-PR pass (#1224 block). That variable is not in the script's opening session-tmp `files` map (`queue-pull-script.md:17` onward), which declares every other `DISPATCH_*` path. The redirect target therefore expands to an empty string, and bash prints `: No such file or directory` on every queue pull. The script has no `set -e`/`set -u`, so execution continues. The message is noise, but it reads as a failure in every `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` run (bare drain or `#N`).

`git grep -n "DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED\|open-pr-excluded" -- plugin` returns only that one line. Nothing reads the file. #1752 moved per-reason exclusion files to the unified `dispatch-exclusions.json` (`plugin/bin/lib/dispatch/exclusions.js`). The open-PR pass now records exclusions via `appendExclusion(…, { reason: 'open-pr' })` into `$DISPATCH_EXCLUSIONS`, which `dispatch/SKILL.md`'s `#N`/`#N,#M` paths read. The line at `:294` is a leftover from that migration.

## Deliverables

1. Delete `echo '[]' > "$DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED"` from `queue-pull-script.md:294`.
2. Add a conformance test to `tests/bin-lib/dispatch/exclusions.test.js` asserting that every `$DISPATCH_*` variable the script references is either declared in its `files` map or assigned in the script. This guards against the same migration leftover recurring.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `queue-pull-script.md` contains no reference to `DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED`.
- The new test fails on the current file, naming `DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED` (verify by running it before the deletion), and passes after it.
- Existing `tests/bin-lib/dispatch/` suites, and any byte-pin or snippet-conformance test over `queue-pull-script.md`, pass. Update a byte pin only if one pins this exact fence, and name it in the PR.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Dispatch no longer prints a spurious "No such file or directory" error each time it pulls the queue.

## Technical Approach

A one-line deletion plus a referenced-vs-declared scan of the script. The original request's proposed diff (preserved below) is a reasonable starting point. Its declaration regex must match the `files` map's actual `KEY: 'file'` lines and any `KEY=` assignments, and the reference regex must cover both `$VAR` and `${VAR}`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md` — delete the dead redirect (`:294`)
- `tests/bin-lib/dispatch/exclusions.test.js` — referenced-vs-declared `$DISPATCH_*` conformance test

## Gotchas

- `queue-pull-script.md` is run verbatim by `/dispatch` Step 2, and some of its fences may be byte-pinned by snippet-conformance tests. Grep `tests/` for the file name before editing.
- `node-eval-file.js` heredoc bodies inside the script reference shell variables through `process.env` or `$VAR` interpolation. Make sure the scan does not flag a variable that is assigned inside a heredoc-fed command as undeclared, or narrow the scan to shell-level references.

## Original request

dispatch: queue-pull-script.md redirects to undeclared $DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED (": No such file or directory" on every pull)

**Summary:** queue-pull-script.md writes to the never-declared $DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED, so every queue pull prints ": No such file or directory"

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** dispatch (skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md)

**Repro steps:**
1. On any project, run `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` (bare drain or `#N`) so Step 2 runs `queue-pull-script.md` verbatim.
2. Watch the open-linked-PR pass (#1224 block).

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: the open-PR pass runs silently; every `$DISPATCH_*` path the script writes is declared in its opening `files` map.
Actual: bash prints `: No such file or directory` on every queue pull. The script has no `set -e`/`set -u`, so execution continues and the error is only noise, but it reads as a failure.

**Root cause:** `skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md:294` runs `echo '[]' > "$DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED"`. A mechanical referenced-vs-declared comparison found it is the only undeclared `DISPATCH_*` variable in the script. Deleting the line is the fix.

**Proposed fix:**

diff --git a/plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md b/plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md
--- a/plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md
+++ b/plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md
@@ -291,7 +291,6 @@ DISPATCH_GROUP_NUMS=$(node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/node-eval-file.js" "$DISPA
 NODE_EVAL_EOF
 )

-echo '[]' > "$DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED"

   if ! node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/resolve-linked-prs.js" "$DISPATCH_GROUP_NUMS" \
     > "$DISPATCH_LINKED_PRS" 2>"$DISPATCH_LINKED_PRS_ERR"; then
diff --git a/tests/bin-lib/dispatch/exclusions.test.js b/tests/bin-lib/dispatch/exclusions.test.js
--- a/tests/bin-lib/dispatch/exclusions.test.js
+++ b/tests/bin-lib/dispatch/exclusions.test.js
@@ -104,3 +104,20 @@ test('AC5: an unknown reason round-trips through readExclusions but is only matc
   assert.equal(groupIsExcluded([{ number: 42 }], entries, ['oversized', 'firing']), false);
   assert.equal(groupIsExcluded([{ number: 42 }], entries, ['future-reason']), true);
 });
+
+// #1752 left one write to a retired per-reason file behind in queue-pull-script.md's open-PR pass
+// (`echo '[]' > "$DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED"`) after its declaration left the session-tmp files map,
+// so bash redirected to an empty path and printed `: No such file or directory` on every pull.
+// Every $DISPATCH_* the script references must be declared in that map or assigned in the script.
+test('queue-pull-script.md: every referenced $DISPATCH_* variable is declared or assigned', () => {
+  const script = fs.readFileSync(
+    path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', '..', 'plugin', 'skills', 'dispatch', 'queue-pull-script.md'), 'utf8',
+  );
+  const referenced = new Set([...script.matchAll(/\$\{?(DISPATCH_[A-Z0-9_]+)/g)].map((m) => m[1]));
+  const declared = new Set([
+    ...[...script.matchAll(/^\s*(DISPATCH_[A-Z0-9_]+):\s*'/gm)].map((m) => m[1]),
+    ...[...script.matchAll(/\b(DISPATCH_[A-Z0-9_]+)=/g)].map((m) => m[1]),
+  ]);
+  const undeclared = [...referenced].filter((v) => !declared.has(v));
+  assert.deepStrictEqual(undeclared, [], `undeclared variables: ${undeclared.join(', ')}`);
+});
```

**Test:** extend `tests/bin-lib/dispatch/exclusions.test.js` (in the diff): asserts every `$DISPATCH_*` the script references is declared in its `files` map or assigned in the script. Fails on current `main` naming `DISPATCH_OPEN_PR_EXCLUDED`; passes after the deletion, and guards future migration leftovers.

**Related:** #1752 (closed; the migration that left this line behind).

**Definition:** Clear

entries.title: Windows regression: 1 test file(s) newly failing after c65b3fdbb
entries.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #3392, #3429, #3440, #3505, #3506, #3507, #3509, #3518, #3523

## Current State

The post-merge `windows-regression` workflow (run 39103544055, on `windows-latest`) flagged `tests/dispatch-neighbour-in-flight-mcp.test.js` as newly failing after PR #3441 merged as `c65b3fdbb` (#3392's MCP-transport branch for dispatch's neighbour-in-flight pass). That merge added the file, so it has no earlier Windows baseline. The run's `verify-report` artifact lists it as the only `attributable` file. The other 102 files failing at head were already failing at base `2514e406c`.

The issue excerpt quotes one failure. The run's `tests` log shows four of the file's six tests failing, all with the same assertion:

- `AC1.1: the MCP claim-target snippet prints [9] …` (line 81): `heredoc #0 has no NODE_EVAL_EOF terminator`
- `AC2.1: a stale label with no live claim …` (line 91): `heredoc #1 has no NODE_EVAL_EOF terminator`
- `AC3.1: a failed MCP claim read prints the AUTO line …` (line 99): `heredoc #1 has no NODE_EVAL_EOF terminator`
- `AC3.1: a failed MCP pool list is documented to write [] …` (line 109): `heredoc #0 has no NODE_EVAL_EOF terminator`

The two passing tests (lines 118 and 132) only call `includes` on single-line tokens.

Root cause, checked against the file at `origin/main` `7852fd8bf` (it has not changed since `c65b3fdbb`):

- Lines 18-19 read `plugin/skills/dispatch/mcp-transport.md` and `plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md` with raw `fs.readFileSync(..., 'utf8')`. This repo's `.gitattributes` pins only `tools/upstream-drift/fixtures/**`. A Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` therefore reads both files with `\r\n` line endings.
- `snippet(index)` (lines 33-45) finds a heredoc's end with `text.indexOf('\n' + END, found)`, where `END = 'NODE_EVAL_EOF\n'` (line 23). On CRLF text the terminator line is `\r\nNODE_EVAL_EOF\r\n`, so the search returns -1 and line 43's `assert.notStrictEqual(close, -1, …)` throws. That is the reported error.
- Reproduced on macOS from an `origin/main` tree export. The file passes 6/6 as checked out. After converting the two markdown inputs to CRLF it fails exactly the four tests above, with the same `heredoc #N` messages. Routing both reads through `readText()` makes it pass 6/6 again on the CRLF inputs. This was a CRLF simulation on a POSIX host, not a Windows run.
- Normalizing at read time also matters past the extractor. The extracted snippet is run through `bash -c` (`run`, lines 70-77), and a heredoc carrying `\r` would not match its own `NODE_EVAL_EOF` terminator in bash either.

The repo already has the house fix for this class: `tests/helpers/read-skill.js`'s `readText(absPath)`, which normalizes EOLs (#2763). `skill-prose-conformance-tests` requires every prose suite to read governed markdown through it. This file, added by #3392, does not use it. The production prose (`mcp-transport.md`'s two heredocs at lines 121-124 and 132-141) is correct.

## Deliverables

1. `tests/dispatch-neighbour-in-flight-mcp.test.js` reads `mcp-transport.md` and `queue-pull-script.md` through `readText()` from `./helpers/read-skill.js` instead of raw `fs.readFileSync`. The `fs` import stays, because the fixture helper uses it.
2. The extractor itself tolerates CRLF input, not only the read. `section` and `snippet` take the source text as a parameter, defaulting to `MCP`. `snippet`'s terminator search accepts an optional `\r` before each newline around `NODE_EVAL_EOF`, and the start-anchor and missing-terminator asserts are kept.
3. A new CRLF test case. Build `crlf = MCP.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n')`, then assert for heredocs 0 and 1 that `snippet(i, crlf).replace(/\r\n/g, '\n')` strictly equals `snippet(i)` on the LF text.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -n "fs.readFileSync" tests/dispatch-neighbour-in-flight-mcp.test.js` returns no match, and the file requires `readText` from `./helpers/read-skill.js`.
- [ ] `node --test tests/dispatch-neighbour-in-flight-mcp.test.js` passes on macOS/Linux with 0 failures: the 6 existing tests plus the new CRLF case, with none skipped or removed.
- [ ] Go-red check: temporarily reverting `snippet`'s terminator search to the bare `'\n' + END` form makes the new CRLF case fail, and restoring it makes the case pass again. Do the revert and the restore in the same command.
- [ ] The file passes on `windows-latest`. Prove it before merge by dispatching `gh workflow run windows-regression.yml --ref {branch}` and quoting the run's result for this file. A non-main ref never files an issue. If the dispatch cannot run, say so explicitly. Do not count a CRLF or `path.win32` simulation as a Windows run.
- [ ] No file under `plugin/` changes. `mcp-transport.md` and `queue-pull-script.md` stay byte-identical.
- [ ] `npm test` passes with no new failures compared to `origin/main`.

## Release Note

Fixed a dispatch test that failed on Windows checkouts because of line-ending differences.

## Technical Approach

This is a test-only change to one file. It follows `.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md` ("Build CRLF inputs from the LF text") and `.claude/skills/skill-prose-conformance-tests/SKILL.md` ("Prose reads come from the shared helper", plus the Anti-Patterns row on anchoring an extractor on a bare `\n`). Replace the two raw reads with `readText(path.join(ROOT, 'plugin', 'skills', 'dispatch', …))`. Thread an optional `text` argument through `section`/`snippet`, and make the terminator search CRLF-tolerant with a regex or an equivalent pair of `indexOf` probes. Add one `test()` for the CRLF case. Keep `run`'s `bash -c` input LF: every snippet the suite executes comes from the `readText`-normalized `MCP`.

Alternative rejected: a `.gitattributes` `eol=lf` rule for `*.md`. It would change checkout behavior for every Windows user of the repo, and the only `.gitattributes` rule today is a narrow fixture-hash carve-out. `readText()` is the convention that #2763 settled on and that sibling records #3429, #3440 and #3507 apply.

### Key Files

- `tests/dispatch-neighbour-in-flight-mcp.test.js` — use `readText()` for the two markdown reads, parameterize `section`/`snippet` on the source text with a CRLF-tolerant terminator, and add the CRLF case
- `tests/helpers/read-skill.js` — unchanged; the existing `readText()` helper being consumed
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/mcp-transport.md` — unchanged; read-only input (the `## Step 2 — neighbour-in-flight pool (#3278, #3392)` section's two heredocs)
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md` — unchanged; read-only input

## Gotchas

- Scope is this one file. Each sibling "Windows regression: N test file(s) newly failing after …" record (#3429, #3440, #3505, #3506, #3507, #3509, #3518, #3523) covers its own commit and files.
- `tests/dispatch-named-target-exclusion-fixture.test.js` also extracts a `NODE_EVAL_EOF` heredoc. The same run shows it failing at both base and head, so it is a pre-existing Windows failure and not part of this record. `tests/dispatch-per-record-groups-prose.test.js` uses the same `'\nNODE_EVAL_EOF\n'` terminator shape and passed on this run. Leave both alone here.
- Do not run CRLF text through `bash -c`. The CRLF case compares extractions only. A `\r`-bearing heredoc fails in bash for a reason unrelated to the extractor, and that failure would be misread as a regression.
- ubuntu CI cannot see this failure class. The CRLF case is the pin that runs on Linux. Without it, a later edit could reintroduce the raw read or the bare-`\n` terminator and stay green on every PR.

entries.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #3393, #3429, #3440, #3505, #3506, #3507, #3509, #3517, #3523, #2767, #2713, #3024, #3187, #3396, #3500

## Current State

The post-merge `windows-regression` workflow (run 39104307191, on `windows-latest`) flagged two test files after PR #3421 merged #3393 (the chained claim reader) as `f6e30ca84`. The run's `verify-report` artifact (`baselineAdjudicated`, base `8356f387f`) breaks it down per test:

- `tests/dispatch-per-record-groups-prose.test.js`: 10/10 pass at base; 11/13 at head. Both new failures are tests that #3393 added: `AC2.1: the neighbour-in-flight heredoc runs offline …` and `AC1.1: the neighbour-in-flight heredoc reports a failed claim read …`.
- `tests/specify-near-duplicate-prose.test.js`: 10/11 at base; 10/13 at head. The test quoted in this record's excerpt, `the shaping-mode.md refusal fence runs and refuses nothing … (#3141)`, **already failed at base** with the same `refusal fence anchors must exist` error. The new failures are #3393's two tests: `AC1.1: the shaping-mode refusal fence reads claims through createClaimReader …` and `AC1.1: an unreadable claim is reported on the output …`.

There are two root causes, both test-side. Verified against `origin/main` at `7852fd8bf`; the only commits since `f6e30ca84` that touch these files (#3366, #3405) changed neither cause.

1. **CRLF anchors (near-duplicate suite).** `tests/specify-near-duplicate-prose.test.js:18` reads skill markdown with a raw `fs.readFileSync`. On a `core.autocrlf=true` checkout, `plugin/skills/specify/shaping-mode.md` arrives with `\r\n` endings, so the fence anchor `'node -e "\n'` (line 96, and again in `refusalFenceBody` at line 147) never matches `node -e "\r\n`. That fails the #3141 test at line 93 and both #3393 tests at lines 155 and 167. The dispatch suite does not have this problem: it already reads through `tests/helpers/read-skill.js`'s `readText`, which turns `\r\n` into `\n`.
2. **Native path spliced into JS source (both suites).** The tests run a skill's embedded node snippet by replacing `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` with `path.join(ROOT, 'plugin')`: `tests/dispatch-per-record-groups-prose.test.js:134` (`neighbourHeredocCode`), and `tests/specify-near-duplicate-prose.test.js:101` and `:170`. The placeholder sits inside a single-quoted JS string (`require('${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/lib/dispatch/in-flight-neighbours.js')`). A Windows path's backslashes therefore become JS escape sequences: `\a` → `a`, `\c` → `c`. The run shows `Cannot find module 'D:aclaude-tweaksclaude-tweaksplugin/bin/lib/dispatch/in-flight-neighbours.js'`. The near-duplicate tests at lines 93 and 167 have the same defect, currently masked because cause 1 stops them earlier.

The repo already has the fix for cause 2: `tests/auto-merge-short-circuit-verdict-backstop.test.js:28` builds `path.join(ROOT, 'plugin').split(path.sep).join('/')` before splicing it into source.

## Deliverables

1. `tests/specify-near-duplicate-prose.test.js`: route the `read` helper (line 18) through `readText` from `./helpers/read-skill`, so every skill read is LF-normalized.
2. `tests/specify-near-duplicate-prose.test.js`: make the #3141 test at line 93 call `refusalFenceBody()` instead of its own inline copy of the anchor (lines 96-101). Give `refusalFenceBody` an optional text parameter, defaulting to `SHAPING_MODE`, and have it LF-normalize that text. Add one assertion that `refusalFenceBody(SHAPING_MODE.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n'))` returns the same fence as the LF read. That is the CRLF extractor case `windows-checkout-test-parity` asks for, and it goes red on Linux if the normalization is removed.
3. Both test files: splice a forward-slash plugin root into the snippet source instead of the native `path.join(ROOT, 'plugin')`. That means `tests/dispatch-per-record-groups-prose.test.js:134` and `tests/specify-near-duplicate-prose.test.js:101` and `:170`. Use one module-level constant per file, built the way `tests/auto-merge-short-circuit-verdict-backstop.test.js:28` builds its `PLUGIN_DIR`.
4. Before opening the PR, grep the two files again for any other `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` substitution or raw `fs.readFileSync` of a skill file, and fix any hit with the same move. Record the grep and its result in the PR body.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `node --test tests/specify-near-duplicate-prose.test.js tests/dispatch-per-record-groups-prose.test.js` passes on macOS/Linux, with no test skipped, removed or weakened.
- [ ] Both files pass on `windows-latest`, including the #3141 test that was already failing at base. Prove it before merge: run `gh workflow run windows-regression.yml --ref {branch}` and quote that run's result for the two files (a non-main ref never files an issue). If the dispatch cannot run, say so explicitly. A `path.win32` simulation is not a Windows run.
- [ ] The new CRLF case fails on Linux when the normalization inside `refusalFenceBody` is removed. Prove it by reverting the normalization temporarily and restoring it in the same command.
- [ ] No file under `plugin/` changes. The skill snippets and `plugin/bin/lib/dispatch/in-flight-neighbours.js` are correct; only the tests' extraction and substitution are platform-dependent.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Fixed five dispatch and specify prose tests that failed only on Windows checkouts.

## Technical Approach

The fix is test-side only, following `.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md`. Two of its rules apply:

- "A test extracts regions from live skill markdown → a CRLF input proving the extractor still finds the region" covers cause 1.
- Its native-path rule covers cause 2. The value spliced into JS source is a module specifier, not a filesystem path a human pastes into a shell. Forward slashes resolve on every platform, which `tests/auto-merge-short-circuit-verdict-backstop.test.js:28` already relies on.

Folding the #3141 test's inline anchor into `refusalFenceBody` leaves one extractor to keep correct instead of two copies. The CRLF case is the only discriminating check available on Linux CI. The separator fix can only be proven red on a real Windows runner, which is why the workflow dispatch is an acceptance criterion.

### Key Files

- `tests/specify-near-duplicate-prose.test.js` — `read` routed through `readText`; the line-93 test reuses `refusalFenceBody`, which takes text and LF-normalizes it; new CRLF extractor case; forward-slash plugin root at lines 101 and 170
- `tests/dispatch-per-record-groups-prose.test.js` — forward-slash plugin root in `neighbourHeredocCode` (line 134)
- `tests/helpers/read-skill.js` — read-only reference: the `readText` helper this record adopts
- `tests/auto-merge-short-circuit-verdict-backstop.test.js` — read-only reference: the existing forward-slash `PLUGIN_DIR` precedent (line 28)
- `plugin/skills/specify/shaping-mode.md` — read-only reference: the refusal fence the near-duplicate suite extracts (lines 115-146)
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md` — read-only reference: the neighbour-in-flight heredoc the dispatch suite extracts (lines 622-623)

## Gotchas

- Keep the scope to the five tests above. `tests/dispatch-neighbour-in-flight-mcp.test.js` is #3517's (a missing `NODE_EVAL_EOF` terminator). Other suites splice `path.join(ROOT, 'plugin')` into code the same way, for example `tests/tidy-release-note-repair-conformance.test.js:83` and `tests/verify-expectations-writer-conformance.test.js:65`; they belong to the Windows baseline or to their own records, not this one.
- Both #3393 `AC1.1` tests depend on `gh` and `git` being unreachable (`env: { ...process.env, PATH: dir }`). On Windows the inherited variable is usually spelled `Path`, and Node's handling of a `Path`/`PATH` pair in a spawned env can leave the original search path in force. If the Windows run shows these tests reaching `gh` (a resolved slug, or a network read), override every case variant of the path variable in the spawned env rather than loosening the assertion.
- Don't fix this in the skill prose. The snippets run under a shell that substitutes `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` itself; this record changes only how the tests emulate that substitution.
- Line numbers above are as of `origin/main` `7852fd8bf`. Re-anchor on content if the files move.

## Original request

Windows regression: 2 test file(s) newly failing after f6e30ca84

The post-merge Windows check failed on commit f6e30ca842199444560ae9a497b3ed97d49eb1e6 (compared against 8356f387f).

**Merged PR:** #3421 (https://github.com/thn-inc/claude-tweaks/pull/3421)

**Run:** https://github.com/thn-inc/claude-tweaks/actions/runs/39104307191

### Newly failing test files

entries.title: Windows CRLF: ten skill-prose tests read governed markdown raw before bare-\n fence extraction
entries.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #3562, #3563, #3565, #3587, #3574

Origin: #3562 Deliverable 4 (run 2026-10-19T212245-record-3562) — sibling files with the same CRLF read-plus-extract shape, kept out of #3562 by its own Gotchas

Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff

## Current State

#3562 fixed `tests/pipeline-run-dir-adoption-anchoring.test.js` for Windows checkouts: it read live skill markdown with a raw `fs.readFileSync(…, 'utf8')` and applied a bare-`\n` fence regex, which matches nothing once `core.autocrlf=true` gives the doc `\r\n` endings. Its sibling grep (`git grep -lE '```(bash|sh|js|json|yaml|yml)?\\n' -- tests tools`), re-run on this record's build branch (base `4dbf60b8d`), finds ten more files with the same read-plus-extract shape that no open record claims (an open-issue search for each filename returns only #3562 itself, which names them as out of scope). Each reads governed markdown raw and extracts with a bare-`\n` anchored regex:

| File | Raw read | Extractor |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/bin-lib/issues/labels.test.js` | line 126 | line 127, `## Canonical LABELS_JSON[\s\S]*?```js\n([\s\S]*?)\n```` |
| `tests/blast-radius-snippet.test.js` | line 17 | line 18, `is one CLI call[^\n]*\n[^\n]*\n\n```bash\n([^`]+)```` |
| `tests/capture-native-branch-guard-shapes.test.js` | line 28 | line 25, ````bash\n([\s\S]*?)```` |
| `tests/harness-health-runaway-section.test.js` | line 13 | line 27, ````bash\n\s*node -e '…' ` |
| `tests/init-port-isolation-conformance.test.js` | line 13 | line 90, an exact fenced `ports.js allocate` line |
| `tests/plan-audit-check-e-prose.test.js` | line 17 | line 72, `## Invocation\s+```bash\n([^\n]+)\n```` |
| `tests/tidy-release-note-repair-conformance.test.js` | line 10 | line 81, then runs it with `bash -c` (lines 85-86) |
| `tests/dispatch-firing-exclusion.test.js` | line 24 | line 30, then runs it with `bash -c` (line 58) |
| `tests/multispec-not-run-callsite.test.js` | line 22 | line 46, then runs it with `bash -c` (line 96) |
| `tests/verify-expectations-writer-conformance.test.js` | line 16 | line 54, then runs it with `execFileSync('/bin/sh', …)` (line 66) |

Per #3562's Current State, all ten fail on `windows-latest` with an extractor-not-found message. Four of them also run what they extract, so a second Windows layer can sit behind the CRLF one, as #3517, #3555, #3565 and #3587 found: `\r` left in a captured snippet breaks `bash -c`; a native backslash `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` interpolated into a heredoc turns into JS escapes; and a literal `/bin/sh` resolves to `<drive>:\bin\sh` on win32 and throws `ENOENT`. #3565's sweep records `verify-expectations-writer-conformance.test.js:66`'s `/bin/sh` spawn as masked behind the CRLF extraction failure, with no open record owning it.

## Deliverables

1. For each of the ten files above, read the governed markdown through `tests/helpers/read-skill.js`'s `readText()` instead of a raw `fs.readFileSync`. Leave every extraction regex as it is — `readText()` normalizes at the read, so an extracted snippet is LF and runnable on every checkout.
2. For each file that runs what it extracts (`tidy-release-note-repair-conformance`, `dispatch-firing-exclusion`, `multispec-not-run-callsite`, `verify-expectations-writer-conformance`), check the second layer and fix it test-side: a forward-slash `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` where one is interpolated into a script, and no literal `/bin/sh` spawn target (`verify-expectations-writer-conformance.test.js:66` — use `bash` from the inherited `PATH`, as the sibling `bash -c` suites that pass on `windows-latest` do).
3. Add one CRLF control per extractor, built from the LF `readText()` value with `.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n')` (assert `\r\n` present and no `\r\r\n`), proving the read-plus-extract path returns the same result as for the LF text — the pattern #3562 added to `tests/pipeline-run-dir-adoption-anchoring.test.js`.
4. Before opening the PR, re-run the sibling grep above and re-check open records; drop any file another record claims by then and record the grep output in the PR body.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each of the ten files passes `node --test` on macOS/Linux with no test removed, skipped or weakened, plus its new CRLF control.
- [ ] CRLF simulation on macOS/Linux: a scratch copy of `tests/` and `plugin/` with the governed docs converted to `\r\n` fails the pre-fix files with their extractor messages and passes the fixed files. Quote both runs' `# pass` / `# fail` lines in the PR body.
- [ ] All ten files pass on `windows-latest`. Prove it before merge by dispatching `gh workflow run windows-regression.yml --ref {branch}` and quoting each file's per-test `ok` lines from the run's log, not the adjudication verdict alone (a dispatch baselines against `HEAD^1`, #3568). If the dispatch cannot run, say so explicitly.
- [ ] Each new CRLF control discriminates: replacing its `readText(` with a raw `fs.readFileSync(…, 'utf8')` turns it red. Run each doctoring in the same command as its restore.
- [ ] No file under `plugin/` changes.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Fixed ten skill-prose tests that failed only on Windows checkouts because of line endings.

## Technical Approach

Test-side only, following `.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md`'s "Build CRLF inputs from the LF text" pattern and its Anti-Patterns row "Treating a CRLF fix as the whole Windows fix for a test that extracts and runs a skill's shell snippet". `readText()` is the repo's single EOL-normalizing read for governed markdown; `skill-prose-conformance-tests` already requires it for every prose suite. Normalize at the read, not with a `\r?\n`-tolerant regex: a suite that runs its extracted snippet would still hand `bash -c` a snippet full of `\r` (reproduced in #3562's scratch run).

### Key Files

- `tests/bin-lib/issues/labels.test.js`, `tests/blast-radius-snippet.test.js`, `tests/capture-native-branch-guard-shapes.test.js`, `tests/harness-health-runaway-section.test.js`, `tests/init-port-isolation-conformance.test.js`, `tests/plan-audit-check-e-prose.test.js` — read-only extract-and-compare suites: route the read through `readText()`, add a CRLF control
- `tests/tidy-release-note-repair-conformance.test.js`, `tests/dispatch-firing-exclusion.test.js`, `tests/multispec-not-run-callsite.test.js`, `tests/verify-expectations-writer-conformance.test.js` — extract-and-run suites: `readText()` read, CRLF control, and the second Windows layer
- `tests/helpers/read-skill.js` — read-only reference: `readText()`
- `tests/pipeline-run-dir-adoption-anchoring.test.js` — read-only reference: #3562's CRLF control shape
- `.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md` — read-only reference

## Gotchas

- Do not add a `.gitattributes` `eol=lf` rule for `tests/` or the skill files; the parity skill scopes it to the hashed upstream-drift fixtures on purpose.
- Do not build a CRLF case from a raw read: on a Windows checkout that yields `\r\r\n` (#3523). Build it from the `readText()` value.
- The second-layer failures are inferred for most files, not observed: the CRLF extractor failure masks them on Windows today. Investigate whatever shape the dispatched Windows run shows; never add a win32 skip to turn a run green.
- If this proves too large for one PR, split it along the read-only / extract-and-run line — the four extract-and-run files each need their own Windows proof.

entries.title: archive-run: commits the archive move on the current branch without reporting the commit or that it is unpushed
entries.body:
Surface: terminal

## Current State

`hooks.js archive-run --run <dir>` calls `archiveRunDir` (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`). When the run's `work/` is git-tracked, that function `git mv`s it into `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/archive/` and commits on the main checkout's current branch (`archive-merged.js:1302`, `[reconcile] archive run {runId}`, scoped to its own paths per #2241). The function returns only `{ ok: true, movedEntries }` (`archive-merged.js:1503`), so the CLI (`plugin/bin/hooks.js:1249-1252`) prints the `moved: …` lines and `claude-tweaks: archived {run-id}`. Nothing tells the caller that a commit landed, on which branch, or that it is unpushed.

Observed twice:
- In a consuming project (the original request below): the silent commit left local `master` ahead of origin, and a deploy script hard-stops on that.
- In this repo on 2026-10-21: a `/claude-tweaks:sweep` run archived 69 run dirs via `archive-run`. Four of them carried tracked `work/` and produced four unreported `[reconcile] archive run` commits on local `main` (`d48c523e0`, `6cf4efb34`, `325facfe8`, `d447003fe`). They were only noticed through a manual `git log`.

#3396 tracks the broader mechanism (unpushed reconcile archive commits on the main checkout). This record is the output gap only, which is separately fixable.

## Deliverables

1. `archiveRunDir` reports the commit it made: on success with a commit, its return value carries `commit: { sha, branch }` (short sha of the `[reconcile] archive run` commit, plus the checked-out branch name). `commit` is absent when no tracked content moved and no commit ran.
2. `hooks.js archive-run` prints one line after `archived {run-id}` whenever `commit` is present: `claude-tweaks: committed {sha} on {branch} (not pushed — {n} ahead of {upstream})`. When the branch has no upstream, the parenthetical reads `(no upstream configured)`. When the ahead-count probe fails, it reads `(push state unknown)`. The line never fails the verb.
3. The reconcile archival path that calls `archiveRunDir` surfaces the same `commit` field in its per-run result entry, so `hooks.js reconcile --json` consumers see it too.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Archiving a fixture run with tracked `work/` returns `commit.sha` matching `git rev-parse --short HEAD` after the call, and `commit.branch` matching the checked-out branch. Archiving a fixture with no tracked content returns no `commit` field.
2. `archive-run` stdout on a tracked-work fixture contains a line matching `/^claude-tweaks: committed [0-9a-f]{7,} on \S+ \((not pushed — \d+ ahead of \S+|no upstream configured|push state unknown)\)$/m`. On an untracked-only fixture, stdout contains no `committed` line.
3. The ahead count is correct: a fixture whose branch tracks an upstream at the pre-archive commit reports `1 ahead`.
4. The reconcile `--json` run entry for an archived tracked-work run includes the `commit` object.
5. Existing `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js` cases still pass unchanged, including the `moved:`-line cases.

## Release Note

archive-run now tells you when it commits the archive move, on which branch, and whether that commit is still unpushed.

## Technical Approach

Capture the commit's sha right after the successful `commitGit` call in `archiveRunDir`, using `git rev-parse --short HEAD` plus `git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD` through the same `runGit` seam, and thread it into the success return. In `hooks.js`, compute the ahead count with `git rev-list --count @{upstream}..HEAD` (anchored `-C mainRoot`), degrading to the two fallback parentheticals. Reconcile's archive call site copies the field into its result entry. Pushing, or skipping the commit on the integration branch (the request's optional alternatives), is out of scope. Those are behavior changes that belong to #3396's mechanism decision.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `archiveRunDir` returns `commit: { sha, branch }` after a successful commit; the reconcile call site (around line 1870) carries it into the run entry
- `plugin/bin/hooks.js` — `archive-run` prints the committed/ahead line
- `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js` — new stdout assertions for the committed line
- `tests/reconcile.test.js` — `archiveRunDir` return-shape assertion for `commit`

## Gotchas

- `archive-run`'s stdout is documented as informational human text that no caller parses (`hooks.js` comment above `archiveRunDir`), so adding a line is not a contract change. The `--json` run-entry field is additive.
- Resolve the ahead count from `mainRoot`, not from `process.cwd()`. A worktree cwd has a different HEAD (`[IL-127]`-style shadowing).
- An unborn or detached HEAD has no symbolic ref. Report the branch as `detached` rather than throwing.

## Original request

archive-run: commits the archive move on the current branch without reporting the commit or that it is unpushed

**Summary:** `hooks.js archive-run` commits the archive move on the main checkout's current branch, but its output never mentions the commit or that it is unpushed.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** `bin/hooks.js archive-run` → `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` (around line 1169)

**Use case:**
After `close-run`, `hooks.js archive-run --run <dir>` was run in the main checkout, which was on the integration branch (`master`). It `git mv`'d the run's `work/*-spec.md` files into `pipelines/archive/` and committed them as `[reconcile] archive run <run-id>`. The commit is correctly scoped to its own paths (#2241). The CLI output listed only `moved: …` lines and `archived <run-id>`. It never said that a commit was made, on which branch, or that the commit was not pushed.

In this project, local `master` being ahead of `origin/master` is a hard stop for the deploy script, which refuses to run until the commit is pushed. The remote host's nightly backup also commits and pushes without pulling, so a push made later, but not deployed, can leave that backup's push rejected. The commit was only noticed by chance (`git worktree list` showed `master` at a new SHA), and it took a push plus a deploy to clear.

Repro:
1. Main checkout on the integration branch, in sync with origin.
2. `hooks.js close-run --run <run-dir>`, then `hooks.js archive-run --run <run-dir>` for a run whose `work/` holds tracked spec files.
3. `git status -sb` now shows `ahead 1`, but nothing in the archive-run output said so.

Suggested change: have `archive-run` (and the reconcile pass that calls the same code) report the commit in its output, for example `committed <short-sha> on <branch> (not pushed — <n> ahead of <upstream>)`. Optionally, offer a `--push` flag, or skip the commit when the checked-out branch is the integration branch and leave the moves staged with a note. At minimum, say that the commit exists.

Related: #3396 tracks the same symptom in this repo: unpushed `[reconcile] archive run` commits on the main checkout's local `main`. Its Deliverable 2 asks which mechanism leaves them there. This report is that mechanism seen from a consuming project, plus the output gap, which is fixable separately.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.145.0

---
Filed via /claude-tweaks:feedback.
<!-- fingerprint: feedback-07ce1823 -->

## Plan Review Decisions

Decided by the maintainer on 2026-11-02, who accepted these readings in session. Where a decision conflicts with the text above, the decision wins.

- **A commit followed by a refusal: Reading B.** Declare `archiveCommit` before the commit, have `refuseAfterMarker` carry it, have `archive-run` print the committed line on refusal too, and have reconcile's `skipped` entries copy it. Add a test using the stray-file fixture. This extends Deliverable 1 beyond the success path.
- **`commit` when a post-commit probe fails: Reading A.** AC2 stays as written, so no placeholder sha may reach the line. On a failed sha probe, retry or print a different line. Use `detached` only on `exitCode === 1`.

Origin: ledger resolve gate from #3687 (items 6 and 22)
Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

`tests/ledger-reader-ownership-conformance.test.js` (#3687) fails the suite when a this-run ledger lookup in an instruction step reintroduces the bare `docs/plans/*-ledger.md` glob. It scans one sentence at a time, and three escapes were found by the build's final review and the review lenses (3f pair, 3a): `ALLOWED_RE` exempts any sentence that merely contains "fallback", "inherited", "unattributed" or "other run's", so a reintroduced this-run glob in a sentence that also says "fallback" passes; `GLOB_RE` matches only the literal `docs/plans/*…-ledger.md` spelling, so `docs/plans/*ledger*.md`, the dated `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-*-ledger.md` shape, or `find docs/plans -name "*-ledger.md"` pass; and the sentence splitter merges across a lowercase continuation, so a glob sentence can inherit an exempting word from its neighbour. Closing all three needs a different scan shape (a structural check of which steps are this-run lookups, rather than sentence-level word matching), so it was not fixed inside #3687. ## Acceptance Criteria
